question: Two Singapore companies are each 80% owned by the same Hong Kong-incorporated parent. Can one of them set its current-year losses against the other's profits?
evidence: at least 75% of the total number of issued ordinary shares in each of the 2 companies are beneficially held, directly or indirectly, by a third Singapore company

question: A subsidiary closes its books on 31 March but its sister company has a 31 December year end. Can unused capital allowances be passed from one to the other?
evidence: the transferor and claimant must have the same accounting year end to qualify for group relief.

question: A company filed its return showing a profit, but IRAS's assessment turned the result into a loss. How long does it have to file the form needed to pass that loss to a sister company?
evidence: must submit a Form GR A within 2 months from the date of the notice of assessment which shows that it has loss items available for transfer

question: The profitable subsidiary wants to pay the loss-making subsidiary for the tax losses it absorbs. Can the payer deduct that payment, and is it taxable for the company receiving it?
evidence: it would not be entitled to claim a tax deduction for such payment. Likewise, the transferor would not be subject to tax on such a payment.

question: A new company makes its first sale in March 2024 and has a 31 December year end. How far back before 1 January 2024 can its revenue expenses still be deducted?
evidence: at any time before the date the person derives that first dollar of income, but no earlier than 12 months before the first day of the applicable basis period

question: In its first year a company earns both normally taxed income and income taxed at a concessionary rate. How are its set-up costs from before trading began deducted when they cannot be traced to either income stream?
evidence: The remaining pre-commencement expenses and s14R expenses will be allocated to the respective income streams based on income apportionment.

question: Can a company whose property investment business is taxed under section 10D deduct revenue expenses it incurred before it earned any rental income?
evidence: Subsection (1) does not apply to the business of making investments carried out by a company or trustee of a property trust, to which section 10D applies.

question: A start-up's deductible expenses from before it opened are larger than the income it earns in its first year. What can it do with the unused amount?
evidence: Any excess of the pre-commencement expenses or s14R expenses over the respective income streams would form part of the trade losses

question: What facts will IRAS ask for when working out the date on which a company's business actually began?
evidence: (iii) whether the company has begun its day-to-day business operations; and (iv) chronological list of key events leading up to the profit-making structure being operationally ready

question: My client spent its first year negotiating its main supply contract, arranging bank financing and building its factory. Has it started business for tax purposes?
evidence: Such activities may include signing a business contract, obtaining a loan to build infrastructure for the business and construction/building of the infrastructure.

question: Why are costs a business incurs before it starts operating generally not deductible under the general deduction rule?
evidence: All outgoings and expenses incurred prior to the date on which a business commences operation are not wholly and exclusively incurred in the production of income.

question: An asset manager began pitching its funds to prospective clients in March 2019 but only received its first fee in January 2020. When does IRAS treat its business as having started?
evidence: The business of fund management commenced on 15.3.2019 when the company was able to market its products and services.

question: How much of this year's unused capital allowances and trade losses can a company set against the previous year's assessable income?
evidence: restricted to the lowest of: (i) your actual amount of the QD; (ii) your assessable income of the immediate preceding YA; and (iii) $100,000.

question: A sole proprietor with other assessable income in YA 2017 started a new business in the basis period for YA 2018 and ended that first period with both a trade loss and unused capital allowances. Can both be carried back to YA 2017?
evidence: you will not be able to carry back the unabsorbed CA granted for the first basis period that you commenced a trade, business or profession.

question: By when must a company elect to set this year's loss against last year's income, and can it withdraw the election afterwards?
evidence: Any election made under subsection (6) is irrevocable and must be accompanied by such particulars as the Comptroller may require.

question: A company is transferring part of its current-year loss to a sister company and wants to set the rest against its own income of the previous year. How is the amount it can carry back worked out?
evidence: the amount of QD you can carry back is the net amount after deducting the loss items transferred out to the eligible claimant company or companies.

question: From YA 2025, how much fit-out and refurbishment spending on business premises can be claimed, and over which block of years is that limit measured?
evidence: the relevant three-year period for claiming R&R expenditure will be fixed for all businesses, with the first fixed three-year period being from YA 2025 to YA 2027

question: A client closes its business for good partway through the three-year write-off of its office fit-out costs. What happens to the deduction for the remaining years?
evidence: ceases permanently during the basis period for that YA, no S14N deduction is to be given in that YA.

question: A sole proprietor runs his business from one room of his flat and refurbished the whole flat. Can he claim part of the cost under the renovation deduction?
evidence: If you cannot specifically identify the R&R expenditure to the area used for business purposes, you are not allowed to claim S14N deduction

question: Can the fees paid to an interior designer for an office makeover be included in the renovation deduction?
evidence: any designer services or professional services, except designer services or professional services which do not affect the structure of the business premises from YA 2025

question: What does s 14N(4) say about renovation costs a business incurs before it starts operating?
evidence: is deemed to have been incurred by that person on the first day that person carries on that trade, profession or business

question: What does s 37D(12) require of a company's shareholders before it can carry back its capital allowances or trade losses?
evidence: not less than 50% of the total number of issued shares of the company are held by or on behalf of the same persons

question: What does s 14X(4) provide when a business's first-year income is entirely concessionary or entirely tax-exempt?
evidence: comprises only concessionary income or only exempt income, the expense is to be deducted against that income.

question: Under section 37C, in what order are a loss-making company's capital allowances, trade losses and donations passed to the claimant company?
evidence: The loss items of a transferor are transferred out in the order as follows: 1: Unabsorbed capital allowances for current year 2: Unabsorbed trade losses for current year

question: Under section 14Q, can a client write off its renovation costs in one year instead of over three years, and can it change its mind later?
evidence: From YA 2025 onwards, the option to claim qualifying R&R expenditure in one year instead of over three years will be permanently available to businesses
